replies.body:
Thanks for the suggestions!

Does those suggestions relate to an existing semconv recommendation regarding metric names ? For example, I don't recall seeing the pattern of "using plural noun" elsewhere, at least in the jmx metrics. I now we have something explicit about this in the choice of nouns as unit.

I think doing this would introduce something that is inconsistent with the current [tomcat](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation/jmx-metrics/library/tomcat.md) or [activemq](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/blob/main/instrumentation/jmx-metrics/library/activemq.md) metrics for example.

I have to admit that we have a lot of `.count` suffixes, this comes from the exposed MBeans (which is relying on yammer metrics for kafka), and doing so allows to easily extend if needed.

For example, with `kafka.log:type=LogFlushStats,name=LogFlushRateAndTimeMs` MBean:
- we capture `Count` attribute as `kafka.log.flush.count` to get the number of flushes
- the `Mean`, `50th` or `99th` attributes is also exposed and provides respectively the average, so we could potentially use `kafka.log.flush.duration.{average,p50,p99}`
- if we use `kafka.log.flushes` for the flush count, then we could not use `kafka.log.flushes.duration.*` without having the count metric be a prefix of the duration metrics.

The otel weaver have [a rule](https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/blob/main/test_data/attribute_name_collisions.rego) about avoiding namespace collisions, but there is nothing about metric names. I don't recall exactly the context in which I added this recommendation as part of the [JMX metrics recommendations](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/tree/main/instrumentation/jmx-metrics#jmx-metrics-definitions-recommendations), so it is definitely possible that I inferred this recommendation from what we have with metric attributes (but at least it would be consistent).

For suggested attributes renames:

- `kafka.topic` --> `kafka.topic.name` : this is fine, I'll change it.
- `kafka.isr.operation` --> `kafka.server.isr.operation` seems a bit redundant as isr is only used in the `kafka.server` namespace, I'll leave it as-is for now.

found the following semconv issues/PRs that relate to avoiding prefixes conflicts for metric names here: 
- https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/issues/2419
- https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/pull/2492

for pluralization, check out https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/general/naming.md#pluralization

there's nothing conflicting about:

```
kafka.log.flushes
kafka.log.flush.duration.p50
kafka.log.flush.duration.p99
```

`kafka.topic.name` follows object/property naming guidance in https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/general/naming.md#general-naming-considerations

for adding `server` to `kafka.isr.operation`, see https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/general/naming.md#signal-specific-attributes

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include zero-valued per-topic failure series**

When `kafkaBrokerZookeeper()` runs against Kafka 2.8.1, creating a per-topic `BrokerTopicMetrics` instance registers both failure-rate MBeans even when their `Count` is zero, and the JMX callback records those zero observations. Consequently `kafka.server.failed_requests` contains fetch/produce points for every created topic, not only produce/`my-compacted-topic`; because `hasDataPointsWithAttributes` rejects every point not covered by a supplied group, this assertion (and the analogous new per-topic assertions above) cannot pass. Include the zero-valued topic/type combinations or use matchers that accept all emitted topics.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
